author: Buckethead
content: Alright since we just established the superiority of 2handed tanking I want to talk some more about dw tanking. Like I described earlier I want to mostly go 1-hand + shield and swap out the shield during combat for an offhander when I need more rage. The mainhander's weapon swing would be uninterrupted so it should be seamless. Then I just swap back when I have enough rage. Towards the end of each fight, when damage is small, I could also stay in def stance with dw and just build some rage for the next fight (most of the time I want to pull the next pack rather than charge anyway, so no need to change stances). My question is, would I need to go all the way into anger management in the arms tree? I do want to pick up at least 3 of the tactical mastery points so I don't lose my charge rage but I don't really see the need for anything more than that. I'll have all I need in defensive stance, the only thing i need battle stance for is charge and mocking blow. This kind of talent build is what I have in mind starting out: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/warrior/50I-55 EDIT: The 1 rage/3sec seems valuable though. My thought behind this whole thing is to play something more tanky and easy on the healer than 2h arms but have an edge when I would otherwise get rage-starved and lose aggro. I fully understand I should go 2h arms but it ruins my nostalgia.

author: Aubreykun
content:
There is some custom twow gear that seems designed for PvP. Includes mostly offensive stats with some defensive interest, such as (the crafted) Pauldron of Deflection.

If you're "undergeared" then you need to play smart and not zug. For wpvp I find that wars are batman classes - you need to have your head on a swivel and swap to items and strats that will help you with your chosen target. 

This means using things to:
- pop rogues out of vanish. AoE damage (like un'goro crystal bombs if you're not an engineer, or thunderbrew's boot flask, or chained essence), phantom blade, alliance faerie fire candles, etc.
- additional gap closers against kitey mages and hunters like the ulda charge helm or rocket helmet, discombobulator ray, swiftness potions/stopwatch, ornate mithril boots
- making sure you're in zerk stance when fighting locks to pop zerk rage
- if you have it, choosing select pieces of gear with additional shadow/arcane resist against mage/lock to prevent them from CC-ending the fight by running away

Without raiding, if you want the epic swordsmith sword - [Tempered Runeblade] - and all this other capability, your BEST option is likely to level as gnomish engineer, then swap to bsmith near 60 and do the sword - it requires crafting AND a quest - then swap to goblin engineering once you made it.

author: Panfusion
content:
So obviously arms is better in PvP with mortal strike debuff and more high end burst potential but this is why I like fury/arms pvp:

1. More consistent rage gen 
2. Heroic strike is better dw than 2h
3. More spell cast pushback
4. overpower is up very often due to fast oh and improved overpower is nearly a guaranteed flurry proc.
5. Improved berserker rage allows you to use other rage gen sources and always be able to intercept (or cast battle shout at the end of a battle with sub 10 rage).
6. improved execute is sick in pvp (often times I can execute high armor folks twice in 1.5s since it's only 10 rage and if I get both swings in I got at least 10 more).
7. Fury arms is better than deep arms while using shields (which is pretty relevant in pvp to be able to swap.
8. Deathwish is good vrs many matchups and gives you an easy fear break while in defensive/battle stances.

author: Aubreykun
content:
```for warrior tanking, with a shield you only need 2% block and + 7 defense from items to be uncrushable/uncrittable vs bosses that attack slow enough to have 100% shield block uptime.

You need 102.4% total avoidance to be uncrushable.
5/5 Anticipation puts you at 310 defense, and you need 315 for your full 5% each of Miss/Dodge/Block/Parry. That totals 20%. 

Shield Specialization (which you need 5/5 of for Improved Shield Block anyway) gives an additional 5%.

And then a lot of shields - as well as the enchant - give 2% block.

So, really all you need is 7 Def.... and a lot of shields and other equipment give 7 def.

Of particular note, Aegis of the Blood God gives exactly 2% block and 7 Defense, leaving its enchantment slot open for 7 stamina. A few other shields give either block or defense, so the other portion is intended to come from gear.```

author: Forlorn Shade
content:
@Deleted User 
Responding to https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/466622456308957205/1361968502340321434 here since it's more appropriate than there.
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/warrior?points=FQRAQYDQpSAABABoAoBYAoAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=
You want to have full Tactical Mastery, because there are a number of Abilities in the 20-25 bracket for Rage Cost. It also sets you back less with each Stance swap you do, which is also just a passive positive.

Improved Charge is awesome going from enemy to enemy whenever ready, as you get some nice, bug refills.

Counterattack sucks big time, especially when considering the filler Points you need to spend just to get to it. No use getting it. Use Deflection as a filler just to get lower along the Talent Tree.

Slam can be useful, but its Cast Time is atrocious without its Talent. Should get it. This way, you can swing > Improved Slam > Ability > swing and repeat, a lot easier. You also do not avoid attacks mid-Cast-Time, which sucks for having a slower one, thus, shortening it helps reduce how much you open yourself up (you can still move and thus kite with it).

You can either stick to Unbridled Wrath 5/5 with Booming Voice 1/5, or get BV to 5/5 and Improved Shouts 1/5. Reasonings are: Hamstring CD sucks, thus a wide Piercing Howl can help, plus you can use Intimidating Shout from much farther (can be clutch), as well as having to spend less Rage and fewer Global Cooldowns on refreshing Battle/Demoralizing Shout; UW at 1/5 is too low to be worthwhile anymore, so you might as well give a small boost to Shouts with Improved as a filler to get down one more Tier on the Talent Tree.

You could also get 2/2 Reckless Execute and 3/5 Enrage, so you can have Execute at the ready always, but the overall Damage dip from a weaker Enrage can be offputting. Either works (you probably shouldn't be spamming Execute from Mob to Mob while leveling, due to draining your Rage, and starting new fights with nothing).

author: Virasan
content:
“Any recommended arms talents/builds for leveling?” (UPDATED FOR 1.18*)

I see this question asked in here constantly. There is no “best” leveling build. Most people will tell you “go arms it’s the best leveling spec”. Others will say “dual wield gets really good around 40 on twow with the cc2 changes” or “I just wanna level in prot”. Honestly you can do whatever you want and you should; it’s just a game after all. Why do you want to follow a cookie cutter build anyways? All that said, a good number of people end up wanting to do so anyways.  

In an effort to address this common question, here is my recommended arms leveling talents:

Cruelty 5/5
Improved rend 2/2
Tactical mastery 3/5
Improved thunderclap 1/3
Improved charge 2/2
Tactical mastery 5/5
Improved overpower 2/2
Deep wounds 3/3
Two-handed weapon specialization 3/3
Impale 2/2
Sweeping strikes 1/1
Master strike 1/1
Master of arms 5/5
Improved slam 2/2
Improved thunderclap 2/3
Mortal strike 1/1
Unbridled wrath 5/5
Improved shouts 5/5
Enrage 5/5

Now I’m sure a bunch of people will come in and say “You should respec at 30 for sweeping strikes, or at 40 for mortal strike”. You are probably right. In fact, people can and will have endless  arguments about what order of talents is best, but most those people won’t actually sit down and write you out a list to follow like people ask, because then they have to expose themselves to the criticism of others by having an opinion. The reason I choose this order of talents is that it requires no respecing since a lot of people don’t have or want to spend the gold while leveling. It also has a few picks that won’t be optimal as a level 60 dps raiding build…. Because that’s not what it is. This is for people leveling with arms. Thunderclap may suck in a raid setting but it’s actually not terrible early on and is still a nice utility aoe you can use in addition to battle and demo shouts when your tanking in arms as a sub 60 or working on pre raid.

author: Velanir
content:
**Threat Multipliers**

Threat multiplier stances (baseline):
> T_defStanceBaseline = 1.3
> T_battleStanceBaseline = 0.8

Multiplier Defiance (5/5):
> T_defiance = 1.2

Calculation for defensive stance threat with Defiance:
> T_defStance = T_defStanceBaseline * T_defiance
> T_defStance = 1.56

Calculation for Defensive Tactics multiplier:
> This is **NOT **the final threat multiplier. This multiplier will get multiplied with the base threat multiplier of battle stance in the next step. 
> **without **Defiance:
> T_defTactics = (T_defStanceBaseline - 1) * 1.8 + 1
> T_defTactics = 1,54
> **with **Defiance:
> T_defTacticsDefiance = (T_defStance - 1) * 1.8 + 1
> T_defTacticsDefiance = 2,008

Final multiplier in battle stance:
> **without **Defiance:
> T_battleStance = T_battleStanceBaseline * T_defTactics
> T_battleStance = 1,232
> **with **Defiance:
> T_battleStanceDefiance = T_battleStanceBaseline * T_defTacticsDefiance 
> T_battleStanceDefiance = 1,6064

TL/DR: Defiance is getting applied even when using battle or berserker stance with defensive tactics.
The talents do stack.
Battle/Berserker Stance + Defiance + DTactics =  1,6064
Defensive Stance + Defiance = 1.56

author: Raphael
content:
I swapped at 40 and have zero issues holding threat.
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/warrior?points=FQQDKYAQ--UYAoIAAohQAYB
This isn't optimal AT ALL but I like if for running dungeon pugs (YMMV) for various reasons
Prot side is standard.
In Arms, I like Charge and Imp. Clap because randoms are just going to full send it on every pull and I like to guarantee I rocket up the threat table regardless what they do.
I like Master Strike, its useful to have another option sometimes when the other party members arent doing anything other than spamming their DPS buttons. And i think its cool and have one of each weapon and a swap macro for each. Keeps things interesting, like a little mini-game I play just for me.

I stay mainly in battle stance on trash.
Mark Skull > Charge > Demo Shout > Thunder Clap > Conc Blow > Shield Slam > Sunders  [Overpower on procs]
Then I either throw in more Claps if they are not focusing the skull, or SS and put up 2 Sunders between its cooldown.
Rarely have more that 4 mobs on trash in 5 mans, healer never pulls threat, some warriors do if they out gear/level me, they can take it till i pull threat back off.

Bosses I do the same but swap to Def Stance after initial Charge to let the healer take a breather and use Revenge on Proc

author: Black Hat
content:
Hey everyone,

We never thought we’d be writing a message like this—but here we are.

As many of you know, a recent bug allowed all PvP warriors to disorient players by using Mace Master Strike for the whole duration, regardless of whether they recieved damage or not. For a brief, beautiful moment, Warriors across Turtle were finally united—not by frustration, but by joy. People were excited to log in. Our discord was alive. PvP felt fun again.

And then changelog took it away.

They didn’t celebrate the renewed interest. They didn’t lean into the excitement. Instead, they doubled down on one of the most player-hostile design philosophies still haunting this game: Nerfs. If you weren’t there at the right patch, at the right time, under the right moon phase, tough luck. No sparkles for you.

We get it. Some skills are meant to be balanced. But what we saw this patch wasn’t gamebreaking or actually made warriors viable in pvp — it was a harmless bug that reignited love for a space that’s spent years in the shadows. Devs could’ve used it as a moment to bring the community together. Instead, they chose nerfs over fun.

So, we’re done.
Effective immediately, the Warrior Discord will be locked down and archived. This is a symbolic gesture—a protest—not just against this decision, but against the design mentality that drives it. We won’t keep pretending this is fine. We won’t help Devs gatekeep fun.

Thanks to everyone who made this community what it was. We hope to daze again someday, when the game is worthy of its players.

Catch y’all later.
— Kyrsie

author: Nost
content:
These were some calcs I did a while ago to see how good BV is, as I wasn’t sure how accurate the guide was, if you see any errors lmk. 

1 SBV contributes to 1 damage, Shield Slam has a 1.5x damage to threat modifier and a base damage of 350. Shield Slam also has a 0.15 Attack power modifier. SS scales with str,crit & block value. So, to look at how much threat 1% crit , 1 strength, 1 BV provide: 

1% crit = 350 (damage at 0 ap) x 1% (chance of crit happening) x 1.5 (threat modifier on SS) x 1.2 (impale talent)= 6.4 more threat 

1% crit (at 1000ap) = 350 + 0.15 (SS AP modifier)*1000 x 1% x 1.5 x 1.2 = 9 more threat 

1 block value = 1 damage on SS x 1.5 (threat modifier) x 1.15 (toughness talent) = 1.73 extra threat. so at 5.2 block value you get 9 threat

1 strength = 2 ap x 0.15 (SS AP modifier) x 1.5 = 0.45 threat (1str also provides 0.05 bv (0.087 threat) so is actually 0.537 threat) so at 18.8 st you get 9 threat

so 1% crit provides, 18.8 st or 5.2 bv worth of threat on shield slam assuming you have 1000ap already. For reference my current gear has 930 atm.

At 0 ap 1% crit = 3.7 BV or 12 st worth of threat. So the more AP I have the more valuable crit becomes. And vice versa, the more crit I have the more valuable strength becomes.

Okay so for defensive tactics threat BiS this is basically the highest reasonable threat setup that I could come up with.
- Apocalypse leggings perform ~4 tps better which means they aren't reasonable

- BoUF performs ~5 tps better than Qirajy Fury but doesn't offer any stamina
- Applied Forces is the next best performing ring after Qiraji Fury (if you were to value dodge, you would value it above Qiraji Fury)
- Glyph + Kiss outperform any MotC combination in all relevant scenarios 
- Thunderfury outperforms all other options
- RC and THC are the next best options after TF with RC having higher average threat but THC having significantly better consistency. Therefore TF > THC > RC would be a reasonable assumption 
- Thunderfall is trash, don't even think about taking it

author: Guts
content:
Arp, isnt a stat worth pursuing as

A: Its a numerical Value compared to % based which your probably know from wotlk

B: It only has an effect some of the time (meaning alot of bosses get to 0 armor with common debuffs used in Classic raiding)

Then as to crit vs haste 

There's one of Warrior's most overpowered Talents called Impale which increases the damage bonus from critical strikes on skills, so crit has additional value compared to other classes (Flurry aswell in fury but we're talking arms here). Deep Wounds isnt as powerful in this Version but its still free damage (a tiny incentive for crit again).

Crit will scale with EVERYTHING you do (Strength does aswell, except execute), while haste only affects a certain percentage of your Damage. Another Reason why crit is so good for warriors is because Classic wow's system of not having crit value but instead having percentages of crit is just balanced poorly.

I could go on, but if you want to figure these things out for yourself i recommend playing around with some simming.

content:
--------- Easiest slam macro ----------
```
#showtooltip Slam
/startattack
/cast [noslamclip] Slam
```
Requirements tho
```
SuperWoW - modificiation
SP_SwingTimer - addon 
[SuperCleveRoidMacros](https://github.com/jrc13245/SuperCleveRoidMacros) - addon 
```
------ Older version and that require manual calcuation + macro edit whenever u swap weapon -------

```#showtooltip Slam
/startattack
/run if st_timer>UnitAttackSpeed"player"*0.9 then CastSpellByName("Slam") end
```
Requirements
```
SuperWoW - modificiation
SP_SwingTimer - addon 
```
Now important part u replace *0.9 with your own number

```SLAM CAST TIME / BASIC MAIN HAND WEAPON SPEED```

Your weapon swing speed can be checked via script below to account for some atack speed / haste enchants

```/script local mh, oh = UnitAttackSpeed("player"); print("MH:", mh, "OH:", oh)```

In my case cast its 2.45 default SLAM cast speed and 3.45 Weapon Speed
```2.45/3.45 = 0.71```
